name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.exists_liftedCornerExponential_apply_eq_involution
title: Lifting a corner involution to an ambient CAR unitary

content.display_title: Lifting a corner involution to an ambient CAR unitary
content.one_sentence_role: A prescribed unitary involution on a represented root corner can be realized on finitely many vectors by one lifted corner exponential.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra: the norm completion of the increasing union of $A_n=M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ under the unital embeddings $a\mapsto a\otimes I_2$ (with the fixed coordinate reindexing). Write $\iota_n:A_n\to A$ for the canonical isometric inclusion and $e_{ij}^{(n)}=\iota_n(E_{ij})$ for its matrix units. Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space and $\rho:A\to B(H)$ an irreducible unital star representation. Fix a stage $n$, put $e=e_{00}^{(n)}$, and let $R=\operatorname{ran}\rho(e)$. Suppose $U:R\to R$ is a surjective complex-linear isometry with $U^2=I_R$. For a finite family $v_0,\ldots,v_{d-1}\in R$, there is $h=h^*\in A$, supported by $e$ on both sides, such that the unitary $u=\sum_i e_{i0}^{(n)}\bigl(e\exp(ih)\bigr)e_{0i}^{(n)}$ satisfies $\rho(u)v_j=Uv_j$ for every $j$.
content.assumptions: The Hilbert space is complete and nonzero; irreducibility here means that the representation has no proper nonzero closed reducing subspace. The integer $d$ may be zero. The selected vectors need not span $R$. The involution is defined on the whole corner Hilbert space and is unitary there.
content.conclusion: The same supported self-adjoint generator gives the ambient unitary and all the prescribed finite actions. Support means $eh=h=he$. The sum amplifies the corner unitary $e\exp(ih)$ to a unitary of the unital algebra $A$.
content.proof_summary: The involution determines an orthogonal projection $Q=(I_R-U)/2$. Let $T$ be the zero extension of $\pi Q$ from $R$ to $H$, where $\pi$ denotes the real circle constant. On the finite span of the selected vectors and their images under $U$, $\exp(iT)$ acts as $U$. Supported self-adjoint interpolation realizes this exponential by a corner element; matrix amplification preserves its action on root-corner vectors.

proof_steps.text: Since $U$ is a unitary involution, $Q=(I_R-U)/2$ is an orthogonal projection. Let $T$ be the zero extension of $\pi Q$ to $H$. It is self-adjoint, has range in $R$, and leaves the finite-dimensional space $E=\operatorname{span}\{v_j,Uv_j\}$ invariant. On $R$, $\exp(i\pi Q)=I_R-2Q=U$.

The supported exponential interpolation result gives a self-adjoint $h\in eAe$ whose corner exponential acts as $\exp(iT)$ on $E$. Its proof first interpolates $T$ on $E$ with $\|h\|\leq2\|T\|$, then uses invariance of $E$ to compare the exponentials there.

For $z=e\exp(ih)$, the matrix-unit amplification $L_n(z)=\sum_i e_{i0}^{(n)}ze_{0i}^{(n)}$ is unitary. On a root-corner vector its represented action reduces to that of $z$. Hence $\rho(L_n(z))v_j=Uv_j$. The route explanation below records the accompanying stage-central paths separately.

content.lean_realization_notes: Only the displayed finite family is required to have the prescribed action. The theorem does not identify the action on the whole corner with $U$, and does not give a small-norm bound for $u-1$. In this Hilbert-operator setting the source adjoint $T^\dagger$ is the ordinary Hilbert adjoint $T^*$; the exact source notation is retained.
